metadata.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Word-word co-occurrence matrix $X$
nodes.statement_latex: Let $X$ be the matrix of word-word co-occurrence counts, with entries $X_{ij}$ tabulating the number of times word $j$ occurs in the context of word $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Matrix $X$ has entries $X_{ij}$ counting how often word $j$ appears in the context of word $i$.

nodes.name: Row sum $X_i$ and conditional probability $P_{ij}$
nodes.statement_latex: Define $X_i = \sum_k X_{ik}$ (the number of times any word appears in the context of $i$) and $P_{ij} = P(j\mid i) = X_{ij}/X_i$ (the probability that word $j$ appears in the context of word $i$).
nodes.statement_clean: Row sum $X_i$ totals contexts of word $i$; $P_{ij}$ is the conditional probability of $j$ given context $i$.

nodes.name: Word vectors $w$ and context vectors $\tilde{w}$
nodes.statement_latex: Let $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$ denote word vectors and $\tilde{w} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ denote separate context word vectors.
nodes.statement_clean: Each word has both a target vector $w$ and a context vector $\tilde{w}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Co-occurrence probability ratio
nodes.statement_latex: The co-occurrence probability ratio is $P_{ik}/P_{jk}$, used to probe the relationship between target words $i, j$ via probe word $k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Ratio $P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ measures discrimination between target words via probe $k$.

nodes.name: Weighting function $f$
nodes.statement_latex: Weighting function $f(x) = (x/x_{\max})^{\alpha}$ if $x < x_{\max}$, and $f(x) = 1$ otherwise. Used with $x_{\max}=100$ and $\alpha = 3/4$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounded power-law weighting function for co-occurrence counts; saturates at $x_{\max}$.

nodes.name: Softmax probability $Q_{ij}$
nodes.statement_latex: $Q_{ij} = \exp(w_i^T \tilde{w}_j) / \sum_{k=1}^{V} \exp(w_i^T \tilde{w}_k)$, the softmax probability that word $j$ appears in the context of word $i$ (skip-gram / ivLBL).
nodes.statement_clean: Softmax form of the context-word probability used by skip-gram and ivLBL.

nodes.name: Generalized harmonic number $H_{n,m}$
nodes.statement_latex: $H_{n,m} = \sum_{r=1}^{n} 1/r^m$, the generalized harmonic number.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard generalized harmonic number used in complexity analysis.

nodes.name: General functional form for ratio
nodes.statement_latex: $F(w_i, w_j, \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ (Eqn. 1): the most general form linking three word vectors to a probability ratio.

nodes.name: Vector-difference functional form
nodes.statement_latex: $F(w_i - w_j, \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ (Eqn. 2): restrict $F$ to depend on the vector difference of target words.

nodes.name: Dot-product reduction
nodes.statement_latex: $F((w_i - w_j)^T \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ (Eqn. 3): take the dot product to map vectors to a scalar without mixing dimensions.

nodes.name: Homomorphism condition
nodes.statement_latex: $F((w_i - w_j)^T \tilde{w}_k) = F(w_i^T \tilde{w}_k) / F(w_j^T \tilde{w}_k)$ (Eqn. 4): require $F$ to be a homomorphism from $(\mathbb{R},+)$ to $(\mathbb{R}_{>0},\times)$.

nodes.name: Solving for $F(w_i^T \tilde{w}_k)$
nodes.statement_latex: $F(w_i^T \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik} = X_{ik}/X_i$ (Eqn. 5), with $F = \exp$ as the solution.

nodes.name: Log form of inner product
nodes.statement_latex: $w_i^T \tilde{w}_k = \log(P_{ik}) = \log(X_{ik}) - \log(X_i)$ (Eqn. 6).

nodes.name: Symmetric log model with biases
nodes.statement_latex: $w_i^T \tilde{w}_k + b_i + \tilde{b}_k = \log(X_{ik})$ (Eqn. 7): add bias terms to absorb $\log(X_i)$ and restore exchange symmetry.

nodes.name: GloVe weighted least squares cost
nodes.statement_latex: $J = \sum_{i,j=1}^{V} f(X_{ij}) \big(w_i^T \tilde{w}_j + b_i + \tilde{b}_j - \log X_{ij}\big)^2$ (Eqn. 8): the GloVe weighted least squares objective.
nodes.statement_clean: Weighted least squares cost summed over all nonzero $(i,j)$ co-occurrences.

nodes.name: Skip-gram global cross-entropy form
nodes.statement_latex: $J = -\sum_{i=1}^{V} X_i \, H(P_i, Q_i)$ (Eqn. 13): the skip-gram global objective rewritten as a weighted sum of cross-entropies.

nodes.name: Squared-log objective with general weights
nodes.statement_latex: $\hat{J} = \sum_{i,j} f(X_{ij}) \big(w_i^T \tilde{w}_j - \log X_{ij}\big)^2$ (Eqn. 16): equivalent (up to bias terms) to the GloVe cost in Eqn. 8.

nodes.name: Power-law model of co-occurrence frequency
nodes.statement_latex: $X_{ij} = k / r_{ij}^{\alpha}$ (Eqn. 17): the number of co-occurrences modeled as a power law in the frequency rank $r_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Corpus size in terms of harmonic number
nodes.statement_latex: $|C| \sim \sum_{ij} X_{ij} = \sum_{r=1}^{|X|} k/r^{\alpha} = k\, H_{|X|,\alpha}$ (Eqn. 18).

nodes.name: Corpus-vocabulary asymptotic relation
nodes.statement_latex: $|C| \sim |X|/(1-\alpha) + \zeta(\alpha)|X|^{\alpha} + O(1)$ (Eqn. 21).

nodes.name: Learn word vectors from corpus statistics
nodes.statement_latex: Given a corpus, learn word vectors $w_i, \tilde{w}_j \in \mathbb{R}^d$ that capture semantic and syntactic regularities — in particular, that linear vector arithmetic such as $w_{\text{king}} - w_{\text{queen}} \approx w_{\text{man}} - w_{\text{woman}}$ holds.
nodes.statement_clean: Learn word vectors so that linear arithmetic encodes word analogies.

nodes.name: Word analogy task
nodes.statement_latex: Given an analogy ``$a$ is to $b$ as $c$ is to ?'', find the word $d$ whose representation $w_d$ is closest (cosine similarity) to $w_b - w_a + w_c$. Dataset: 19{,}544 questions split into semantic and syntactic subsets.
nodes.statement_clean: Solve word analogies via vector arithmetic, evaluated on 19{,}544 questions.

nodes.name: Word similarity task
nodes.statement_latex: Given pairs of words with human similarity judgments, score pairs by cosine similarity of their (normalized) word vectors and report Spearman rank correlation. Datasets: WordSim-353, MC, RG, SCWS, RW.
nodes.origin_citation: Finkelstein et al. 2001; Miller & Charles 1991; Rubenstein & Goodenough 1965; Huang et al. 2012; Luong et al. 2013

nodes.name: CoNLL-2003 NER
nodes.statement_latex: Named entity recognition on the CoNLL-2003 English benchmark, with four entity types (person, location, organization, miscellaneous) and BIO2 annotation.

nodes.name: GloVe training algorithm
nodes.statement_latex: Iterative weighted least-squares model that minimizes Eqn. 8 over word and context vectors $w, \tilde{w}$ and biases $b, \tilde{b}$, training only on nonzero entries of the co-occurrence matrix $X$ using AdaGrad.
nodes.statement_clean: Train GloVe by AdaGrad on nonzero co-occurrences with weighting $f$.
input: Co-occurrence matrix $X$ built from corpus with decreasing-distance weighting (word pairs $d$ apart contribute $1/d$)
Initial learning rate $0.05$, number of iterations (50 for $d<300$; 100 otherwise)
output: Final word representation taken as the sum $W + \tilde{W}$

nodes.name: Skip-gram (cited baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Local context-window neural model that maximizes log-probability of context words via softmax (Eqn. 10), trained on-line over the corpus with negative sampling or hierarchical softmax.

nodes.name: CBOW (cited baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Continuous bag-of-words model: predict a target word from its context using a single-layer architecture based on inner products between word vectors.

nodes.name: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA)
nodes.statement_latex: Global matrix factorization producing low-rank approximations of a term-document matrix; used as a baseline factorization-based word representation method.

nodes.name: SVD baselines (SVD, SVD-S, SVD-L)
nodes.statement_latex: Truncated $X_{\text{trunc}}$ retains co-occurrence with the top 10{,}000 most frequent words. SVD takes singular vectors of $X_{\text{trunc}}$; SVD-S of $\sqrt{X_{\text{trunc}}}$; SVD-L of $\log(1+X_{\text{trunc}})$.

nodes.name: AdaGrad
nodes.statement_latex: Adaptive subgradient method for online learning and stochastic optimization; used as the GloVe optimizer.

nodes.name: Build co-occurrence matrix $X$
nodes.statement_latex: Tokenize and lowercase the corpus, build a vocabulary of the top $V$ frequent words, and accumulate $X$ over a context window (default 10 left and 10 right) with $1/d$ distance weighting.

nodes.name: Initialize parameters
nodes.statement_latex: Randomly initialize word vectors $w_i$, context vectors $\tilde{w}_j$, and biases $b_i, \tilde{b}_j$.

nodes.name: AdaGrad updates over nonzero entries
nodes.statement_latex: For each iteration, stochastically sample nonzero entries $(i,j)$ from $X$ and update parameters by AdaGrad on the gradient of the per-entry loss $f(X_{ij})\, (w_i^T \tilde{w}_j + b_i + \tilde{b}_j - \log X_{ij})^2$ with initial learning rate $0.05$.

nodes.name: Combine $W$ and $\tilde{W}$
nodes.statement_latex: Return final word vectors as the sum $W + \tilde{W}$, which typically gives a small boost over either set alone.

nodes.name: Derivation of the GloVe log model from desiderata
nodes.statement_latex: Sketch: starting from Eqn. 1, restrict $F$ to vector differences (Eqn. 2), reduce to a scalar via dot product (Eqn. 3), enforce homomorphism between $(\mathbb{R},+)$ and $(\mathbb{R}_{>0},\times)$ (Eqn. 4), solve to get $F=\exp$ (Eqns. 5--6), and absorb $\log(X_i)$ into biases to obtain Eqn. 7.

nodes.name: Restrict $F$ to depend on the vector difference
nodes.statement_latex: To capture linear structure via vector differences, restrict $F(w_i, w_j, \tilde{w}_k)$ to $F(w_i - w_j, \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ (Eqn. 2).

nodes.name: Reduce vector argument to a scalar via dot product
nodes.statement_latex: Take the dot product to obtain $F((w_i - w_j)^T \tilde{w}_k) = P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ (Eqn. 3), preventing $F$ from mixing vector dimensions.

nodes.name: Impose exchange symmetry via homomorphism
nodes.statement_latex: Require $F$ to be a homomorphism between $(\mathbb{R},+)$ and $(\mathbb{R}_{>0},\times)$, giving $F((w_i - w_j)^T \tilde{w}_k) = F(w_i^T \tilde{w}_k)/F(w_j^T \tilde{w}_k)$ (Eqn. 4) so that swapping $w \leftrightarrow \tilde{w}$ and $X \leftrightarrow X^T$ leaves the model invariant.

nodes.name: Solve $F=\exp$ and absorb log into biases
nodes.statement_latex: The unique solution is $F=\exp$, giving $w_i^T \tilde{w}_k = \log(X_{ik}) - \log(X_i)$ (Eqn. 6); absorb $\log(X_i)$ into a bias $b_i$ and add a symmetric bias $\tilde{b}_k$ to obtain $w_i^T \tilde{w}_k + b_i + \tilde{b}_k = \log(X_{ik})$ (Eqn. 7).

nodes.name: Derivation of complexity bound
nodes.statement_latex: Sketch: model $X_{ij}=k/r_{ij}^{\alpha}$ (Eqn. 17); express $|C|=k\,H_{|X|,\alpha}$ (Eqn. 18); use $|X|=k^{1/\alpha}$ to write $|C| \sim |X|^{\alpha} H_{|X|,\alpha}$ (Eqn. 19); expand harmonic number (Eqn. 20) and conclude $|X| = O(|C|)$ if $\alpha<1$, $|X| = O(|C|^{1/\alpha})$ if $\alpha>1$ (Eqn. 22). Empirically $\alpha=1.25$ gives $|X|=O(|C|^{0.8})$.

nodes.name: Power-law assumption on co-occurrences
nodes.statement_latex: Assume $X_{ij} = k / r_{ij}^{\alpha}$ where $r_{ij}$ is the frequency rank of the word pair $(i,j)$.

nodes.name: Express $|C|$ via generalized harmonic number
nodes.statement_latex: Sum gives $|C| \sim \sum_{ij} X_{ij} = k \sum_{r=1}^{|X|} 1/r^{\alpha} = k\, H_{|X|,\alpha}$, and using $|X| = k^{1/\alpha}$, $|C| \sim |X|^{\alpha} H_{|X|,\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Apply harmonic-number expansion
nodes.statement_latex: Use $H_{x,s} = x^{1-s}/(1-s) + \zeta(s) + O(x^{-s})$ to expand and obtain $|C| \sim |X|/(1-\alpha) + \zeta(\alpha)|X|^{\alpha} + O(1)$.

nodes.name: Case analysis on $\alpha$
nodes.statement_latex: If $\alpha<1$ then the linear term dominates so $|X| = O(|C|)$; if $\alpha>1$ then the second term dominates so $|X| = O(|C|^{1/\alpha})$.

nodes.name: Empirical regime $\alpha=1.25$
nodes.statement_latex: For the corpora studied, $\alpha \approx 1.25$ fits well, giving $|X| = O(|C|^{0.8})$, better than the worst-case $O(V^2)$ and than on-line methods that scale like $O(|C|)$.

nodes.name: GloVe model complexity
nodes.statement_latex: Under the power-law assumption $X_{ij} = k/r_{ij}^{\alpha}$, the number of nonzero entries scales as $|X| = O(|C|)$ when $\alpha<1$ and $|X| = O(|C|^{1/\alpha})$ when $\alpha>1$. For $\alpha=1.25$, $|X| = O(|C|^{0.8})$.
assumptions: Corpora are large enough to apply the asymptotic harmonic expansion
conclusions: GloVe complexity is $O(|C|^{0.8})$ for $\alpha=1.25$, better than $O(V^2)$ and $O(|C|)$

nodes.name: Equivalence of weighted log-squared error and GloVe cost
nodes.statement_latex: Starting from the global skip-gram cross-entropy objective and replacing cross-entropy by squared error of logarithms with a general weighting $f$ yields $\hat{J} = \sum_{i,j} f(X_{ij}) (w_i^T \tilde{w}_j - \log X_{ij})^2$ (Eqn. 16), which is equivalent (up to bias terms) to the GloVe cost in Eqn. 8.
assumptions: Use a general weighting $f(X_{ij})$ rather than $X_i$
conclusions: Resulting objective $\hat{J}$ matches GloVe (Eqn. 8) up to inclusion of bias terms

nodes.name: Properties of the weighting function $f$
nodes.statement_latex: $f$ should satisfy: (i) $f(0)=0$ with $\lim_{x\to 0} f(x)\log^2 x$ finite; (ii) $f$ non-decreasing so rare co-occurrences are not overweighted; (iii) $f$ relatively small for large $x$ so frequent co-occurrences are not overweighted.

nodes.name: Sum $W+\tilde{W}$ as final vectors
nodes.statement_latex: Using $W + \tilde{W}$ rather than $W$ alone reduces overfitting/noise and typically yields a small boost on the analogy task, especially the semantic subtask.

nodes.name: Window size and symmetry effects
nodes.statement_latex: Smaller and asymmetric (left-only) context windows favor the syntactic subtask, while larger symmetric windows favor the semantic subtask. Diminishing returns appear above $\sim 200$ vector dimensions.

nodes.name: Corpus quality vs.\ size on semantic analogies
nodes.statement_latex: Syntactic accuracy increases monotonically with corpus size, but semantic accuracy can be higher on Wikipedia than on the larger Gigaword corpus, likely because Wikipedia covers more city/country analogies and is updated to assimilate new knowledge.

nodes.name: Ice/steam co-occurrence ratios
nodes.statement_latex: For target words $i=\text{ice}$ and $j=\text{steam}$ with probe words $k \in \{\text{solid}, \text{gas}, \text{water}, \text{fashion}\}$, the ratio $P(k\mid \text{ice})/P(k\mid \text{steam})$ takes values $8.9$, $8.5\times 10^{-2}$, $1.36$, $0.96$ respectively, illustrating that the ratio (not the raw probability) discriminates relevant from irrelevant probe words.

nodes.name: King-queen analogy
nodes.statement_latex: The analogy ``king is to queen as man is to woman'' should be encoded by $w_{\text{king}} - w_{\text{queen}} \approx w_{\text{man}} - w_{\text{woman}}$ in the word vector space.

nodes.name: GloVe analogy results (Table 2)
nodes.statement_latex: On the Mikolov word analogy task, GloVe at $d=300$ on a 6B-token corpus achieves Sem.\ 77.4, Syn.\ 67.0, Total 71.7; trained on 42B tokens, GloVe achieves $75.0$ overall, outperforming all baselines.

nodes.name: Word similarity results (Table 3)
nodes.statement_latex: Spearman rank correlations: GloVe (6B) achieves WS353 $65.8$, MC $72.7$, RG $77.8$, SCWS $53.9$, RW $38.1$; with 42B-token training, GloVe outperforms baselines on all five datasets.

nodes.name: NER results (Table 4)
nodes.statement_latex: F1 scores using 50-d vectors: GloVe achieves Dev $93.2$, Test $88.3$, ACE $82.9$, MUC7 $82.2$, outperforming Discrete, SVD, HSMN, CW, and CBOW on Dev/ACE/MUC7 (HPCA slightly higher on CoNLL Test).

nodes.name: GloVe vs.\ word2vec training-time comparison
nodes.statement_latex: Plotted as a function of training time on the same 6B-token corpus, $d=300$, vocabulary 400{,}000, symmetric window 10: GloVe consistently outperforms CBOW and Skip-Gram and obtains the best results irrespective of training time.
